newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian bonds edge lower in thin volume.
newsitem.headline: Belgian bonds edge lower in thin volume.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds followed their European neighbours lower on Wednesday in thin trading with players turning cautious in anticipation of a rate rise in the U.S. and its possible impact in Europe, traders said.

"There will be a rate rise in the United States in the not-too-distant future, but I don't see why we should have a rate hike in Europe," one trader said. "But people are cautious and they will see what happens here when the U.S. rates go up."
Traders noted that the main focus of activity in Belgium was the short to medium term, with one big seller reported in OLO 10, maturing in June 2002.

But they said that overall market volume was very thin, with little on the horizon to fuel a move in either direction other than U.S. weekly jobless claims and February retail sales data due on Thursday and producer prices and industrial production due on Friday.
Jobless claims for the first week of March are seen at 313,000, and retail sales are expected up 0.6 percent.
Producer prices are forecast down 0.1 percent in February and up 2.3 percent year-on-year, with industrial production seen up 0.5 percent.
The yield of the benchmark 2007 OLO was 5.76 percent against Tuesday's closing 5.75, and the spread over Bunds was nine basis points against eight.
The March futures contract was 19 basis points lower at 122.09.
